titles.li: A waystone for a friendly gate
The league asks to winter here
[snow] A caravan out of the snow

texts.li: The snow has closed the roads ahead of a caravan of {FACTION}, and {X_nameDef}, its caravan master, has turned it toward the colony's smoke. The league would sooner sit the weather out by a friendly wall than on the road, {X_pronoun} told {A_nameDef}, and asks for winter quarters {PLACE}, trading from the camp until the roads open.

[snow] A league caravan of {FACTION} came in out of the snow at a crawl, its beasts white to the knees. {X_nameDef}, the caravan master, asked {A_nameDef} whether they might winter {PLACE}: every crate home, the league says, and the crates will not get home through this.

[lowtech] A long string of laden beasts has come down the frozen road behind {X_nameDef}, a caravan master of {FACTION}, and stopped at the colony. The road won't wait, {X_nameDef} says, but the snow says it has to, and the league would winter {PLACE} and trade there until the thaw.

[!lowtech] A league convoy of {FACTION} has pulled off the snowbound road near the colony, chains on its wheels and frost on its canvas, and {X_nameDef}, who runs it, asks {A_nameDef} for winter quarters {PLACE} until the roads are clear. They will trade while they wait, and keep their wardens on watch.

[their:grateful] The league writes the colony in good ink, and {X_nameDef}, a caravan master of {FACTION}, has brought the caravan straight to it rather than winter anywhere else. {X_nameDef} asks {A_nameDef} for quarters {PLACE} until the roads open, as between friends.
[ws:road] With the roads as busy as they are this year and the snow on top of it, {FACTION}'s caravan has given up on the next waystation. {X_nameDef} asks {A_nameDef} for winter quarters {PLACE}.

settled.li: The league's caravan of {FACTION} has gone into winter quarters {PLACE}: the crates stacked into a windbreak, a fire that never goes out, and a trading table already set up with the season's goods.
{FACTION}'s winter camp is up {PLACE}, the beasts blanketed by the stash and a road warden walking the edge of it, and the caravan master's ledger open on the trading table.
The league caravan has settled in {PLACE} to wait for the roads. Beer by the fire, cloth on the table, and every crate counted twice before dark.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the league's drivers, has seen every road in the region and says none of them leads anywhere better than the colony. {X_pronoun} asks whether the colony could use someone who keeps a fair ledger.
{X_nameDef} from the league's winter camp {PLACE} has spent more evenings at the colony's fire than at the caravan's. Tonight {X_pronoun} asked whether {X_pronoun} might stay when the roads open.

farewell.li: [left:waystone] The league's caravan loaded up as the roads opened, and {X_nameDef} stopped at the colony's gate on the way out to leave a carved waystone in its crate, the mark the league puts on a friend's gate. The colony is in the Waystone Book now, in good ink.

[left:waystone] {FACTION}'s winter quarters {PLACE} are empty. On the way past, {X_nameDef} set a crated waystone down by the colony's gate: every league caravan that sees it standing will know the gate is a friend's.
The league's caravan went out at first light, chains rattling and bells on the lead beast, with every crate it came with and a few more. {X_nameDef} promised to stop again next winter.
{FACTION}'s caravan left its winter quarters {PLACE} as soon as the road would take it. The road won't wait, they say, and it didn't.

lines.li: Every crate home, and every crate counted.
The road won't wait, but the snow says it has to.
Good ink for this lot, they've kept their word.
Fair price, and I'll shake on it.
Three days of snow, then the pass opens.
[!lowtech] Check the chains before you sleep.
A word given at the waystone stands.
Blanket the beasts, it's going to bite tonight.

momentLines.li: [carry] Last one for the table, then beer.
[gift] Stand it where the road can see it.
[gift] Good ink, and now a good stone to go with it.

helpTexts.li: [goods] {X_nameDef} set aside a few things from the caravan's crates for the colony and carried them to the edge of the winter camp, by way of thanks for the wall: {THING}.
[goods] The league's caravan had more than it would carry over the pass, and {X_nameDef} left some of it at the edge of the camp for the colony rather than sell it cheap: {THING}.
[tales] {A_nameDef} sat up at the league's winter fire while {X_nameDef} told the story of Harrow Ford and the nine flags, and of every robber the league has written in red since.
[tales] The drivers had a road for every story and a story for every road, and {A_nameDef} came back from their fire knowing which waystations water their beer.

li.label: Spend an evening at their fire
li.tip: The colony goes over to the league's winter fire this evening for beer and the road's news. Recreation for whoever comes; the caravan warms to the colony.

outcomes.li: The colony is going over to the league's fire this evening. {X_nameDef} says the beer is after the count, and the count is nearly done.
Whoever isn't on watch is going to the caravan's fire tonight, and the drivers are already arguing about who tells Harrow Ford.

li.label: an evening at the league's fire
Ask their road wardens to stand with the colony if raiders come
li.tip: The league remembers who robbed it and guards what it keeps. From now on their wardens take up arms against whatever threatens the colony while the winter camp stands.

outcomes.li: {X_nameDef} gave {A_nameDef} the league's word at the colony's gate: if raiders come while the caravan is wintering here, its wardens will be on the wall.
{X_nameDef} looked at the colony's wall and at the caravan's crates, and said a wall that keeps the crates safe is the league's wall too, for the winter.

li.label: Ask to be written in the Waystone Book
li.tip: {A_nameDef} sits with the caravan master over the league's book of fair dealers, and the colony is written in it in good ink. The league's people think better of the colony.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} sat with {X_nameDef} over the Waystone Book while the colony's name went into it in good ink, with every trade of the winter written beside it.
{X_nameDef} opened the Waystone Book on the trading table, wrote the colony in good ink and had {A_nameDef} sign beside it, as the league does.

li.label: Buy a share of their winter stores ({COUNT} silver)
li.tip: Preserved fare the caravan laid in for the winter, at the league's price: one of the drivers carries it over to the colony's gate.

outcomes.li: {X_nameDef} counted out sacks of preserved fare for the colony and the silver into the caravan's chest, both twice, and sent a driver over with the sacks.
{X_nameDef} sold the colony a hard month's fare at a fair price, wrote it in the ledger and had a driver carry it to the gate.
